hooks._timeout_note: 10 s and NEVER more (owner, 2026-09-26). SessionStart hooks block Claude Code's start-up, and the VS Code extension fails the whole start-up at 60 s ('Subprocess initialization did not complete within 60000ms'); it ignores asyncRewake (anthropics/claude-code#96980). 2.0.0 raised this to 120 s to run the automatic-update apply here; that broke VS Code start-up, so the apply no longer runs in this hook - it runs at SessionEnd, detached (gov-update.sh --apply-at-session-end). settings-merge.js clamps it to 10 whatever a template says, and tests/test-sessionstart-budget.sh fails on any SessionStart hook that is slow or registered above its cap.

hooks._note: The automatic-update trigger (2026-09-27). A launcher: a few file tests, one log line, and - only when a verified release is staged or an apply was interrupted - one detached spawn of gov-update.sh --apply-if-ready (nohup, stdin /dev/null, output to ~/.claude/.governance-update/REPORT, no session tokens, nice 19, a 600 s ceiling where `timeout` exists). Returns in about a second (0.5 s idle, up to ~1.5 s under load, MEASURED on Windows); the apply (18-40 s) runs after this session has ended and defers while any other session is live, so the last session to close installs it. pre-session.sh prints the result at the next start. Never at SessionStart: those hooks block start-up, and the VS Code extension fails a start that takes 60 s.

hooks._timeout_note: Raised 15 -> 60 on 2026-09-18, from a measurement, not a guess. This hook renders and PII-gates the file that was just edited; on a loaded machine (25-36 concurrent bash processes) the render+gate+copy path measured 7.4s / 7.9s / 11.1s / 15.9s -- the last one OVER the old 15s budget. A PostToolUse hook killed at its timeout leaves the live file and the publishable bundle silently DIVERGED, which is the exact failure this hook exists to prevent. Per the 2026-09-15 rule (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), the remedy for a slow-but-correct control is a budget it can finish inside, never a watchdog: machinery that supervises machinery costs time on every run, a bigger budget costs nothing until something is genuinely slow. Same fix and same reasoning as governance-guard.sh (10 -> 60) that day.
